slot.brief: Cannizzaro reaction of a given aldehyde: identify which moiety becomes the alcohol and which the acid (no numbers)

stem: The aromatic aldehyde shown undergoes Cannizzaro reaction with concentrated alkali. After acidic work-up, which product pair is formed?
notes: from question bank g5054b2795fcf (verified in job 20261127-132448-d9ce)
working:
Cannizzaro disproportionation: $2\,\text{ArCHO}+\text{OH}^-\rightarrow\text{ArCH}_2\text{OH}+\text{ArCOO}^-$.\nAcidic work-up converts $\text{ArCOO}^-$ to $\text{ArCOOH}$; the para-F substituent is retained.

Independent check: The substrate is 4-fluorobenzaldehyde, which undergoes Cannizzaro disproportionation. Acidic work-up gives 4-fluorobenzyl alcohol and 4-fluorobenzoic acid.
solution: Cannizzaro reaction disproportionates the aldehyde: $$2\,\text{ArCHO}+\text{OH}^-\rightarrow\text{ArCH}_2\text{OH}+\text{ArCOO}^-.$$ Acidic work-up converts the carboxylate to the acid; the para-fluoro substituent is retained. Thus the products are 4-fluorobenzyl alcohol and 4-fluorobenzoic acid.
